entries.scope_note: Alligators as zoological organisms, including historically identified American alligators and contextually supported historical spellings.
entries.exclusions_note: Crocodiles and caimans are not treated as unconditional synonyms.

entries.scope_note: The historical febrifuge bark complex associated with Cinchona plants, including contextually supported quina and quinquina forms.
entries.exclusions_note: The bark complex is not identical to a single modern Cinchona species or every preparation containing bark.

entries.scope_note: The Linnaean taxon Cinchona officinalis rather than the entire historical febrifuge bark complex.
entries.exclusions_note: Generic cinchona and quinquina passages require species-level evidence before assignment.

entries.scope_note: Portuguese proprietary or compounded febrifuge preparations known as Água de Inglaterra.
entries.exclusions_note: Not treated as another name for cinchona bark; recipes and ingredients varied.

entries.scope_note: The historical occupation and role of the engineer, resolved separately from engineering as a field or generic learned expertise.
entries.exclusions_note: Man of science and other learned occupations are not synonyms.

entries.scope_note: Engineers working primarily on fortification, siegecraft, surveying, and other military works.
entries.exclusions_note: Not all historical engineers were military engineers.

entries.scope_note: Physical machines and historically explicit machine analogies, with metaphorical uses retained as passage-level senses.
entries.exclusions_note: Machine metaphors do not make their subjects literal machines.

entries.scope_note: Psychological and philosophical accounts of awareness or conscious mental life.
entries.exclusions_note: Moral conscience and incidental awareness phrases require separate contextual resolution.

entries.scope_note: The ordered universe or nature conceived as an interconnected whole, distinct from a mere book-title occurrence.
entries.exclusions_note: Title-page and bibliographic uses alone do not establish the conceptual sense.

entries.scope_note: The human species under the Linnaean taxonomic name Homo sapiens.
entries.exclusions_note: Generic theological or anthropological uses of human species are resolved separately.

entries.scope_note: Historical conceptions of humanity as a species when the passage does not warrant direct assignment to the modern taxon.
entries.exclusions_note: Not every use is a taxonomic synonym for Homo sapiens.

entries.scope_note: Historical scientific concepts of ordered development or transformation, with biological and non-biological senses distinguished in passages.
entries.exclusions_note: Not treated as an unconditional synonym for transmutation of species.

entries.scope_note: The historical claim that species transform into other species.
entries.exclusions_note: Kept distinct from evolution, development, and ordinary change.

entries.scope_note: Exceptional natural intellectual or creative capacity, including historically explicit accounts of natural genius.
entries.exclusions_note: Grammatical genius, tutelary spirits, intelligence in general, and eugenics are distinct senses or entries.

entries.scope_note: Cognitive capacity or intellect as discussed in scientific, philosophical, and psychological contexts.
entries.exclusions_note: Not interchangeable with genius, measurement practices, or eugenics.

entries.scope_note: Practices intended to quantify mental capacities, performance, or individual psychological differences.
entries.exclusions_note: Intelligence as a concept is not itself a measurement practice.

entries.scope_note: The modern program of directing human reproduction according to claims about heredity and population quality.
entries.exclusions_note: Not treated as equivalent to genius, intelligence, racial classification, or limpieza de sangre.

entries.scope_note: Melancholy as a historical temperament, condition, or disorder, retaining humoral and later psychological distinctions.
entries.exclusions_note: Incidental sadness and black bile as a substance are not automatically identical to the condition.

entries.scope_note: Historical accounts of communicable disease transmission or contagious influence.
entries.exclusions_note: A disease described as contagious is not itself the concept or mechanism of contagion.

entries.scope_note: Electrical attraction, charge, current, and related historical physical phenomena.
entries.exclusions_note: Metaphorical electricity and particular electrical instruments are separately resolved.
